target_customer: Energy and infrastructure operators (power line, pipeline and railway owners) that pay for inspection data
problem: Helicopter and drone inspections of long linear infrastructure are polluting, costly or short range. HyLight flies hydrogen-powered autonomous airships with sensors for long, precise inspection runs.
business_model: Inspection as a service with own hardware, data platform and reports
product_category: Autonomous airship drones for infrastructure inspection

founders.name: Martin Bocken
founders.background_notes: YC page: engineering background and says he launched several entrepreneurial projects before.

founders.name: Josef Rokusek
founders.background_notes: YC page: foundation in mechanical engineering and sustainable energy.

founders.name: Thomas Laporte
founders.background_notes: YC page: business development with utilities. The YC bio says the three hold masters degrees in mechanical engineering, computer science and business from a French engineering and business school; the school is not named.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to build an airship with fuel cell power, autonomy and regulatory approval for flights near infrastructure. The company says it built 20 HyLighters by its YC listing, which is hardware, aviation and software work together.

defensibility.rationale: Airship hardware, flight approvals and utility contracts (Enedis named in press) are hard to copy quickly, but the inspection data service competes with helicopters and conventional drones.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sources found no incumbent building a comparable airship. Customers named on the site include SNCF, Enedis and VINCI-backed LEONARD supports the company. No acquisition found.

market_need_then: Operators must inspect long networks regularly and methane leak and vegetation rules push for frequent checks. The 2024 round announcements describe the decarbonisation of aerial inspection as the pitch; no dated spend figure was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses hylight.aero rather than a .com, per the company website.

identity.mascot_or_character: The product is called the HyLighter, a named airship

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in IEEE Spectrum, tech.eu and aviation trade press about the airship; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable product object (an airship) draws press, and the name hints at hydrogen and light, but no source states the origin or shows brand-led growth.

outcome_analysis: HyLight raised about 3.7 million euros in April 2024 and 13 million euros in October 2026, and by October 2026 reported four airships in operation with Enedis planning 15,570 km of inspections. The hardware moat and utility pilots helped it raise. The risk noted by Tech Funding News is whether utilities sign contracts large enough to fund a 15 aircraft fleet. No shutdown or sale was found.
notes: The 2024 round is 3.7M euros, reported as about $4M. The 2026 round is 13M euros; no USD figure was stated so amount_usd is null. Sources do not label either round's stage, so stage is other (one summary calls the 2024 round seed). The site also lists Bpifrance, Agoranov, Berkeley SkyDeck, Creative Destruction Lab and LEONARD (VINCI) as backers or supporters, with no amounts. Total of about 16.7M euros is from one summary and not recorded. The competitor search found only 2025 and 2026 landscape pages, so the list is empty. Education: only the unnamed French school is stated.
